sources.entry: FreeAudio - Per-app volume and mute, output device switching, and volume control for HDMI/DisplayPort monitors. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/hakanotal/FreeAudio) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: FreeAudio is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that offers per-app volume and mute, output device switching, and software volume for HDMI/DisplayPort monitors.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a volume slider and mute for each app that plays sound, with app sliders running from 0 to 200% and 100% as the default midpoint. Browser and Electron helper processes are grouped under their parent app. Per-app settings are remembered by bundle ID and applied from the app's first sound, including after a relaunch. It lets you switch output devices and set output volume and mute, and it adds a software volume slider and mute for HDMI/DisplayPort outputs that lack hardware volume. On those outputs it also takes over the volume keys and shows its own HUD. The README says it handles headphones, AirPods and monitors connecting and disconnecting, sample-rate changes, and sleep/wake, and it can launch at login and restart after a crash. It is presented as a free alternative to the paid SoundSource app.
use_cases: control volume of individual apps on a Mac
turn up quiet HDMI or DisplayPort monitor audio
switch audio output between headphones, AirPods and monitors
mute a single app's sound from the menu bar
use volume keys with external monitor speakers
how_to_run: Download the latest FreeAudio .dmg from GitHub Releases (Apple silicon, macOS 27+)
Open the DMG and drag FreeAudio.app to Applications
On first launch, approve the app in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, or run: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FreeAudio.app
Grant System Audio Recording permission when first changing an app's volume
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd FreeAudio, then ./scripts/build-dmg.sh
stack: Private APIs via dlsym (process responsibility, TCC preflight)
notable: Software volume for HDMI/DisplayPort monitors where macOS greys out the volume slider
Uses Core Audio process taps, so no system-wide virtual audio driver is installed
Per-app volume and settings remembered by bundle ID
Zero third-party dependencies, per the README
Sibling project of FreeDisplay with shared foundation
caveats: Requires Apple silicon and macOS 27+ for the release DMG, per the README
App is not notarized, so macOS blocks it on first launch and needs a manual override
Calling apps (FaceTime, Zoom, Teams) should be left at 100% because echo cancellation breaks, and other audio-tap tools can interfere
Level meters and input device control are listed as planned or partial in the README
